levelMapping: Airbnb uses G-levels. G8 'Software Engineer' ≈ Google L4 / Amazon SDE II / Meta E4, typically 2–5 YOE (Blind, Sep 2025: 4.5 YOE = G8; G9 'Senior' needs ~7–8 YOE). G7 is entry (0–3 YOE) and shares the same 'Software Engineer' title, so a ~3.3-YOE candidate can land G7 or G8 depending on demonstrated scope — ask the recruiter for the G-code before the loop. Bengaluru SWE postings (Trust, BizTech) ask 3–5 YOE with ₹30.5–43.5L base, i.e. the G8 band; Senior (G9) India postings ask 7+ YOE at ₹45–65L base. US G8 median TC ≈ $297K (levels.fyi).

process.summary: Airbnb's 2025–2026 loop is: recruiter screen → (for most inbound applicants since mid-2026) an auto-sent CodeSignal 'Industry Coding Assessment' with one 4-level progressive problem → a 45–60 min CoderPad technical screen where code must compile, run and pass tests → a virtual onsite of 4–6 rounds: 1–2 coding rounds, a Code Review round (introduced 2024, replaces the second coding round in many loops), an Architecture/system-design round, a Technical Experience (project deep-dive) round, and 1–2 Core Values interviews (sometimes scheduled as a separate stage after the technical onsite) → hiring committee → team match. Coding is practical and product-flavoured (split-stay listings, menu-combo pricing, terrain + water, Connect Four) with a strong DP/graph skew, and interviewers expect runnable, extensible code rather than pseudocode. Core Values is a true veto round run by trained interviewers from outside the team.

rounds.name: Recruiter / hiring-manager screen
rounds.what: Background, why Airbnb, target team, level under consideration, location/work-authorization and comp expectations. A hiring manager sometimes runs it and asks light technical questions about your projects.
rounds.probes: Whether your interest is specific (product/engineering problem you care about) rather than generic; which tool and session length the next round uses — ask.

rounds.name: Online assessment (CodeSignal ICA)
rounds.what: One stateful implementation problem that grows over four levels (e.g. in-memory cloud storage with users/quotas/compression; banking system with top spenders, scheduled payments, account merges; task manager with quotas and expiring assignments; working-hours register with promotions and double-pay). Starter class skeleton provided; the next level unlocks only when the previous level's hidden tests pass. Proctored: screen share and microphone on. Reported scores like 410/600 and 440/600; many 2026 applicants were rejected after finishing 2–3 of 4 levels. Some older/India loops used HackerRank (LeetCode-style, 60–90 min) instead.
rounds.probes: Clean data modelling that survives Level 3's refactor of Levels 1–2, edge cases (missing accounts, self-transfer, ties broken by id, event ordering by timestamp), correctness over optimality — passing tests is what counts.

rounds.name: Technical phone screen
rounds.duration: 45–60 min (CoderPad; some teams use a shared IDE or whiteboard-with-execution)
rounds.what: One practical problem with a simple first part and a hard extension (e.g. split-stay listing pairs, menu combination pricing, Connect Four, URL query parser, retry wrapper, maximize job reward with deadlines). Code must run against tests you write or that are provided; pseudocode is not accepted. Full-stack/FE reqs get a small widget to build plus product/API discussion. Some loops add a hiring-manager or OOD screen (e.g. implement an Airbnb wallet with runnable tests).
rounds.probes: Time pressure — implement part 1 fast and keep it extensible; dry-run your code on an example; state time/space complexity; interviewers push for the optimal approach even after tests pass.

rounds.name: Onsite coding
rounds.what: One hard, multi-part problem per round, usually dressed in Airbnb's domain: split-stay booking across listings, best downhill ski run (then multiple skiers), terrain rendering + pouring water, cheapest itinerary with a connection limit, minimal set of listings to fit a group, refund allocation across payments, duplicate-account detection. Heavy on DP, graphs/grids, intervals and simulation. Loops without a Code Review round have two coding rounds.
rounds.probes: Follow-up requirements layered on a working solution; whether you acknowledge the change and outline the approach before editing; optimizing a brute force that already passes tests; edge cases (bounds, plateaus, ties).

rounds.name: Code review
rounds.what: Introduced in 2024 as a replacement for the second coding interview in most loops. You are given a small repo for context plus ~3 pull requests of increasing complexity (Python/Go/Java variants exist; PR structure is the same across languages) and write review comments as you would for a teammate. PRs contain planted logic bugs (wrong enum value, off-by-one, dict[key] KeyError, swallowed exceptions), security/authorization issues, missing tests/retries, type-hint and naming problems and duplicated retry logic. Some interviewers stay silent and let you work alone.
rounds.probes: Correctness first, then security, then maintainability/style; calibrating severity (merge-blocking vs nit); explaining why each issue matters and suggesting a fix; speed — candidates report running out of time.

rounds.name: Architecture / system design
rounds.what: Deliberately under-specified Airbnb-domain prompt: booking/reservation with double-booking prevention, listing search, host–guest messaging / group chat, waitlist for hot listings, notification system, job scheduler, distributed KV store, user-event aggregation. One Oct 2026 report mixed HLD with LLD details (Bloom filter, caching). Mid-level (G8) loops always include it; senior/staff loops may have two design rounds.
rounds.probes: Scoping and QPS/scale assumptions; schema and data types; optimistic vs pessimistic locking, idempotency keys, outbox/saga for payment-vs-reservation writes; at-least-once vs exactly-once; what breaks at 10x; DB outage/degradation; monitoring, alerting, SLOs, rollout.

rounds.name: Technical experience (project deep dive)
rounds.what: A focused review of one project you led end to end. Airbnb often sends a prep guide listing the evaluation 'tenets'. Interviewer asks why you were chosen, milestones, delegation, cross-team dependencies, compromises with the PM, testing/monitoring/rollout strategy, what you learned. Interviewers also dig into one-line resume items.
rounds.probes: Separating your individual contribution from the team's ('I' vs 'we'); trade-offs you rejected; measurable impact; accountability and humility when describing conflict — one candidate was rejected for 'speaking poorly of coworkers'.

rounds.name: Core values (historically called 'cross-functional' / 'CV' interview)
rounds.duration: 30–60 min, 1–2 rounds (sometimes a separate stage after the technical onsite)
rounds.what: Run by trained interviewers, often non-engineers from other orgs, against Airbnb's values (Champion the Mission, Be a Host, Embrace the Adventure, Be a Cereal Entrepreneur). Typical prompts: a time you hosted/made someone feel they belong, a risk that could have failed publicly, a time you helped someone with nothing in it for you, community or volunteer contributions, feedback you received, 'Why Airbnb?', what you'd remove from the product.
rounds.probes: Authentic, specific stories (2 per value); concrete product knowledge of the two-sided marketplace; this round is a veto — strong technical scores do not offset a 'no' here.

rounds.name: Hiring committee + team match
rounds.duration: 1–2 weeks typical; reported up to 2–6 months
rounds.what: Debrief and level calibration, then matching with teams that have headcount; backend engineers with distributed-systems experience reportedly match faster. Offers arrive only after a match.
rounds.probes: Communicate competing deadlines clearly; recruiter silence of a week+ between stages is commonly reported.

process.indiaNotes: Contrary to common belief, Airbnb does hire engineers in India: a Bengaluru tech hub was announced in March 2022 ('a few hundred people' initially) and 2025–2026 postings are in-office Bengaluru roles on Trust / Trust & Safety, BizTech (Global Tax Engineering), Tech Foundations and Payments — SWE postings ask 3–5 YOE (₹30.5–43.5L base), Senior 7+ YOE (₹45–65L); a Gurgaon ODC ('Airseva') existed earlier. The India footprint is small and team-specific, so openings at G8 are sparse. Reported India loops follow the same structure (HackerRank or CodeSignal screen/OA → live coding → technical experience → architecture → core values); India screens are reported as unusually hard — 'LeetCode Hard complex DP in 45 min with no hints' (Jul 2025, Oct 2024) — and Taro's small India sample shows 8 experiences with a 13% pass rate. A Blind user with 4.5 YOE was in the India G8 loop in 2025 with DSA + system-design rounds after screening. For US roles Airbnb has a single US pay tier under 'Live and Work Anywhere' (remote-US and SF/Seattle); London is an in-office engineering location; EU remote roles exist via Airbnb Ireland/UK entities (community-known). US/EU roles require local work authorization — confirm visa sponsorship and relocation with the recruiter before investing in the loop, because an India-based candidate will usually be routed to Bengaluru reqs.
process.timeline: 3–5 weeks from recruiter contact to debrief (Glassdoor average 21 days); OA invite arrives within hours of applying; onsite invite ~2 days after a passed screen; team match adds 1–2 weeks in the best case and months when headcount is thin. Re-apply cooloff of ~1 year reported after a reject.
tips: Practise the CodeSignal 4-level format before the OA: you cannot edit the test file, debugging is painful, Level 3 usually forces changes to Level 1–2 code, and passing tests beats optimal code. Centralize entity state (one object per account/user/file) so later levels extend rather than rewrite.
In the phone screen implement the simple first part quickly and make it easy to extend — the hard follow-up is where candidates run out of time. Write your own main()/tests if none are given.

Drill DP and grid/graph problems in Airbnb costumes: split-stay pairs, menu-combo minimum cost (Shopping Offers), minimal listings for a group (knapsack), job scheduling with deadlines, downhill ski run (longest path in matrix), pour water, shortest path to collect keys.

Known questions circulate (Blind: 'everyone knows these questions by now'), but interviewers still ask for optimizations after your brute force passes — pace yourself and don't blurt a memorized answer.
For the Code Review round, read the whole diff first, flag correctness and security issues before style, say which items block merge, and suggest fixes; practise on real open-source PRs for speed.

In system design, lead the scoping; be ready with concrete double-booking prevention (unique constraint/conditional insert, SELECT FOR UPDATE, optimistic version column, Postgres SERIALIZABLE with retries), idempotency keys, outbox/saga, and the strong-vs-eventual consistency split between booking ledger and search.
Pick a wide-scope, cross-team project for the Experience round; practise saying 'I' for your contributions and name trade-offs you rejected; cover testing, monitoring, alerting and rollout.
Prepare two STAR stories per core value plus a community/volunteer story and a concrete 'Why Airbnb' tied to a product problem; the Core Values round is a veto.
Expect slow recruiter communication and a team-match wait; keep other offers warm and share deadlines explicitly.
process.notes: No separate LLD/machine-coding round exists for G8; the design-ish implementation exercises live in the OA (4-level stateful systems), the practical phone screen (wallet OOD, retry wrapper, Connect Four) and the Code Review round — they are listed under 'lld' here. Loop composition varies by team: some 2026 loops still run two coding rounds and no Code Review (Glassdoor Oct 2026, Beijing Sep 2026), some senior loops run two design rounds, and one 2024 team confirmed it skips Code Review. Languages: any mainstream language; code-review PRs come in Python/Go/Java variants. Two Sep 2026 1point3acres threads reference a G8 'AI coding' onsite interview at Airbnb (details paywalled) — ask the recruiter whether AI assistants are permitted or expected in any round; separately, interviewers are reported to watch for unauthorized AI use during screens. Older Airbnb classics (Pancake Sort, Wiggle Sort, Guess the Word, IP→CIDR, Display Pages with host dedup, Prepare the Bunker/meeting scheduler, Minimum Window Substring) did not surface in any 2025–2026 report found; they remain in the LeetCode tag list but the live bank is dominated by the problems listed below.

dsa.title: Split stay: two listings covering a date range
dsa.statement: Each listing has a list of available day numbers (sorted in the screen version, unsorted in a harder variant) and a guest requests nights [S, E]. Return every unordered pair of distinct listings such that one covers a consecutive run starting at S and the other covers a consecutive run ending at E, meeting at some switch day T (S ≤ T < E); a listing that covers the whole range alone is still valid when paired. Output pairs sorted lexicographically, no duplicates. Constraints reach ~2000 listings and 200k availability entries, so per-listing prefix/suffix coverage plus an O(L²) pair check is expected over per-day brute force.
dsa.variant: Technical-screen version gives sorted days; onsite version gives unsorted availability or asks for the 'best' split for a group; interviewers push for optimizing a brute force that already passes tests. A system-design twin ('design the split-stay API') appears in technical screens.
dsa.evidence: Phone screen + onsite reports: LeetCode offer post (2026), Blind DP breakdown (2026), PracHub Sep 2025 / Nov 2025 / Dec 2025 / Jan 2026, 1point3acres featured problem (2026-10)

dsa.title: Menu combinations that sum to an exact bill (decimal prices)
dsa.statement: Given a fixed menu of items with decimal prices (e.g. Fruit 2.15, Fries 2.75, Salad 3.35 …) and a target total such as 15.05, return every multiset of items whose prices sum exactly to the target, or an empty list. Convert to integer cents to avoid float error; prune by sorted prices.
dsa.variant: Follow-ups add quantity limits per item, item variants, or ask for the number of combinations instead of the list; sometimes framed as 'possibleOrders(total)'.
dsa.evidence: Phone-screen reports on LeetCode Discuss and multiple 1point3acres threads ('menu combination', backtracking, quantity constraints)

dsa.title: Minimum cost menu order with combo offers (Shopping Offers variant)
dsa.statement: A restaurant sells n single items with unit prices and m combo offers (fixed quantities of items for one price). Given the exact quantities a customer needs, compute the minimum total cost; you may buy any number of singles/combos but cannot exceed the needed quantity of any item. State = remaining needs tuple; DFS with memoization; base case buys the rest as singles.
dsa.variant: Follow-ups: optimize when only three item types have non-zero need (3-D DP over quantities), prune dominated combos (cost ≥ sum of singles, exceeds needs) and prove optimality is preserved; a Hard 'Minimum Menu Order Cost II' variant is reported in Oct 2026 screens.
dsa.evidence: Phone screen: LeetCode offer post 'most cost-effective menu order' (2026), Blind (2026), PracHub Sep 2025 (two entries), hack2hire 'Minimum Menu Order Cost II' last reported 2026-10

dsa.title: Best downhill ski run from a start cell
dsa.statement: On an elevation grid, a skier starts at a given cell and may move to a 4-neighbour only if it is strictly lower. Return the best run (longest path, with total drop as tie-break in some tellings) and the path itself. Memoized DFS over the implicit DAG; reconstruct the path.
dsa.variant: Onsite follow-up (Jan 2026): extend to multiple skiers starting from different cells — reuse the memo table / design the solution so it extends cleanly; candidate reported the interviewer wanted the multi-skier case handled explicitly.
dsa.evidence: PracHub onsite experience Jan 2026 + question entry (Hard)

dsa.title: Maximum-score path through a checkpoint DAG (ski tournament)
dsa.statement: Skiers go from START to one of several END checkpoints over directed edges [from, to, time]; each checkpoint carries points. Score = sum of points of visited checkpoints minus total travel time. Return the maximum score and print the optimal path. Memoized DFS / DP over the DAG with path reconstruction; discuss BFS/Dijkstra alternatives and why plain Dijkstra fails with rewards.
dsa.variant: Interviewer asks you to compare DFS, BFS and Dijkstra with complexities and dry-run an example within a strict 45-minute window.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Aug 2025 'Maximize path score in DAG'; earlier India coding round (2021) describes the same problem in detail

dsa.title: Render terrain and pour water (ASCII simulation)
dsa.statement: Part 1: given column heights like [5,4,3,2,1,3,4,0,3,4], print the terrain as ASCII with one character per unit of height plus a base row. Part 2: dump q units of water at a column; each unit flows left (then right) to the lowest reachable position per LeetCode 755's rules and settles; print the terrain with water marked. Handle pouring on a peak, pouring at an edge (water spills off), plateaus, and q larger than the basin.
dsa.variant: Candidates must agree flow rules with the interviewer (left-first vs split); full working simulation plus printing is expected in 45–60 min; related Trapping Rain Water (LC 42) is in the same family.
dsa.evidence: Onsite coding in Senior loops Jul–Aug 2024 (1point3acres, Taro Seattle), 1point3acres onsite thread 'terrain and water simulation', PracHub Oct 2025 and Feb 2026 entries, older LeetCode Discuss post

dsa.title: Connect Four / Connect-N engine with win detection
dsa.statement: Implement a drop-token game on an m×n board: players alternate dropping a piece into a column (it falls to the lowest empty row); after each drop report whether that player now has k in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally, detect a full-board draw and reject invalid moves. Expose it as a small API (new game, drop(column) → result, board state) and write tests. Win detection should check only lines through the last-placed cell, O(k) per move.
dsa.variant: Parametrize board size and k ('Connect-N'); design the data structure to detect a winner incrementally; an OOD version asks for the class model of a turn-based grid game; Jan 2026 screen gave an unfamiliar board game whose approach mirrored Connect Four with careful bounds handling.
dsa.evidence: Phone screen reports PracHub Jul–Aug 2025 (3 entries), PracHub Jan 2026 OOD entry and Jan 2026 experience, hack2hire 'Design Connect Four' (Hard, screening), InterviewDB 'Board Game'

dsa.title: Board-game score from connected regions on a grid
dsa.statement: Given a grid representing a finished board game (cells hold a colour/owner and sometimes a value), find all connected regions of same-colour cells and aggregate their cell counts and values into a per-player score under stated rules (e.g. a region scores only if it is enclosed or exceeds a size). Return the scores. Flood fill / union-find over the grid; careful with bounds and tie rules.
dsa.variant: Follow-ups change the scoring rule or ask for incremental rescoring after one move.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Feb 2026 'Compute board-game score from regions'; hack2hire 'Calculate Board Score' (Medium, screening, last reported 2026-10)

dsa.title: Maze score via shortest path (Shortest Path in Binary Matrix variant)
dsa.statement: Given a maze grid with walls, a start and target(s), compute a 'score' for the maze state that is a function of the shortest path length from start past the walls (e.g. remaining moves or points lost per step). BFS over open cells; return a sentinel when unreachable.
dsa.variant: Asked in a Jan 2026 phone screen alongside the board-game problem; candidate compared it to LC 1091.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Jan 2026 experience + 'Compute maze score using shortest path' entry (Hard)

dsa.title: Maximum profit in job scheduling / tasks with deadlines
dsa.statement: Choose non-overlapping jobs (start, end, reward) to maximize total reward for up to 200k jobs — sort by end, DP + binary search. Deadline variant: each task takes one day and has a deadline and reward; maximize reward by scheduling at most one task per day (sort by deadline, min-heap of chosen rewards, evict the smallest when over capacity).
dsa.variant: Phone-screen version provides test cases and 45 minutes; India screens report it as 'LeetCode Hard weighted overlapping intervals' with no hints.
dsa.evidence: 1point3acres phone screen 'maximize task profits given deadlines', PracHub Jul 2025 & Sep 2025, vendor guide 'task scheduling with deadline', Taro India Oct 2024; also #2 in the LeetCode tag snapshot

dsa.title: URL query-string parser
dsa.statement: Parse the query portion of a GET URL into a map of keys to values: split on '&' and '=', percent-decode (%20, %2B …) and treat '+' as space, keep repeated keys as lists in order, handle keys with no value, empty segments, a trailing '#fragment', and malformed escapes without crashing. Then write tests for each edge case.
dsa.variant: Follow-ups: nested keys like a[b]=c, size limits, and re-encoding back to a canonical string; one 1point3acres entry is titled 'URL Parser with Percent Unquote'.
dsa.evidence: Hello Interview lists it as commonly asked at G8 and G9; PracHub Mar 2026 (Senior+); hack2hire last reported 2026-10; InterviewDB 'Query Parser' phone screen; 1point3acres list

dsa.title: Text justification / wrap paragraphs into a bordered box or table
dsa.statement: Variants of word-wrapping: (a) wrap each paragraph at its own width inside one ASCII box and pad lines to a uniform width; (b) print a list of sentences as a bordered table with a fixed content width; (c) tokenize text, wrap within line constraints, then parse queries over it. Greedy line packing with careful space distribution and border drawing.
dsa.variant: Interviewers add widths that differ per paragraph, words longer than the width, and exact border characters; expect to write and run tests on output strings.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Feb 2026 (table), Mar 2026 (layout + query parsing), Aug 2026 (wrapped paragraphs in one box); hack2hire 'Format Articles Within Width' (2026-07); InterviewDB 'Article Formatting'; #3 in LeetCode tag snapshot

dsa.title: Flatten 2D vector / nested-list iterator with remove()
dsa.statement: Implement an iterator over a 2D vector (or arbitrarily nested integer lists, cf. LC 341) with hasNext()/next(), plus remove() that deletes the element most recently returned by next() from the underlying structure, and repeatable peek/lookahead. Keep indices consistent after removal and handle empty inner lists.
dsa.variant: Nested version requires a stack of (list, index) frames; 'one removal per item' rule; asked as the second half of a linked-list screen in Apr 2026.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Jul 2026 'Removable Nested-List Iterator', Apr 2026 'Flatten a Nested Integer List' and 'Linked-List and Iterator Problems'; hack2hire 'Flatten 2D Array With Remove' (2026-09); 1point3acres 'Nested List Iterator with Remove'

dsa.title: Design Excel sum formula / mutable sum-tree with fast queries
dsa.statement: Implement a spreadsheet supporting set(cell, value), get(cell) and sum(cell, ranges) where a sum cell depends on other cells and must stay current as dependencies change (dependency graph with propagation, cycle awareness). A related reported problem: design a tree where each internal node stores the sum of its children and supports point updates and fast subtree-sum queries.
dsa.variant: Hello Interview lists LC 631 as commonly asked at both G8 and G9; PracHub Sep 2025 'mutable sum-tree' is the lighter variant.
dsa.evidence: Hello Interview G8/G9 guides; PracHub Sep 2025; #1 in the LeetCode tag snapshot (100% of last-3-month frequency)

dsa.title: Maximum candies from boxes / tokens from nested crates
dsa.statement: Boxes contain candies, keys to other boxes and other boxes; some start locked. Starting from a set of initial boxes, repeatedly open any box you hold a key for and collect its contents; return the total candies reachable. BFS with sets of held keys and found-but-locked boxes.
dsa.variant: Airbnb costume: 'crates with tokens and keys'; follow-up asks for the order of opening or minimal keys used.
dsa.evidence: Hello Interview G8/G9 'commonly asked'; PracHub Aug 2025 (crates) and May 2026 (candies, locked); #6 in LeetCode tag snapshot

dsa.title: Accounts merge / duplicate account detection via shared identifiers
dsa.statement: Accounts carry a name plus identifiers of several types (email, phone, government id). Two accounts are duplicates if they share any identifier, transitively. Given a target account, return all its duplicates (or group all accounts). Normalize identifiers (case-insensitive email), map identifier→account, union-find over accounts.
dsa.variant: Follow-ups add a new identifier type mid-interview and then a new account that links two existing groups, expecting incremental union-find; 2026 'Account Registration Deduplication' version is onsite Easy.
dsa.evidence: Hello Interview G8 common question; hack2hire 'Account Registration Deduplication' onsite (2026-09); detailed India coding-round write-up on LeetCode Discuss; #11 in tag snapshot

dsa.title: Sliding puzzle (2×3)
dsa.statement: Given a 2×3 board with tiles 0–5 (0 is the blank), return the minimum number of slides to reach the solved state, or -1; return the move sequence in the Airbnb version. BFS over encoded board states with a precomputed neighbour table for the blank.
dsa.variant: Asked to also output the moves, and to discuss A*/bidirectional BFS for larger boards.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Apr 2026 'Solve a Two-by-Three Sliding Puzzle' (Hard); 1point3acres problem list

dsa.title: Palindrome pairs
dsa.statement: Given distinct words, return all index pairs (i, j), i ≠ j, whose concatenation words[i]+words[j] is a palindrome. Hash reversed words and split each word into prefix/suffix palindromic parts for O(n·k²).
dsa.variant: Paired in one Aug 2025 screen with Shortest Path to Get All Keys (LC 864).
dsa.evidence: PracHub Jul 2025 and Aug 2025 entries; long-standing Airbnb tag

dsa.title: Shortest path to get all keys
dsa.statement: On a grid with walls, keys a–f and locks A–F, find the fewest moves from the start to collect all keys; a lock can be passed only with its key. BFS over (row, col, keymask) states.
dsa.variant: Reported as 'collect all keys and pass matching doors' in Jul–Aug 2025 screens.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Jul 2025 and Aug 2025

dsa.title: Cheapest itinerary with a limit on connections (Cheapest Flights Within K Stops)
dsa.statement: Given flight fares between cities and a maximum number of allowed connections, find the lowest-fare route from source to destination and return the itinerary (not just the cost). Bellman-Ford limited to k+1 relaxations or BFS/Dijkstra with a stop budget, with parent pointers for path reconstruction.
dsa.variant: Onsite coding round 1 in a Q3-2024 loop; guides describe it as 'cheapest route with at most K layovers'; InterviewDB lists 'Flight Route' as a phone/onsite problem.
dsa.evidence: 1point3acres onsite write-up (posted Feb 2025), techinterview.org guide (2026-07), InterviewDB; #25 in tag snapshot

dsa.title: Fill a layover exactly with experiences
dsa.statement: A traveller has a layover of fixed length and a catalogue of experiences, each with a duration (possibly fractional hours) and optionally a price/rating. Select experiences whose durations exactly fill the layover (or maximize value without exceeding it); return the chosen set or report impossibility. Convert durations to integer minutes to dodge floating-point error, then subset-sum/knapsack DP with reconstruction.
dsa.variant: 'Determine Exact Layover Booking' (Apr 2026) stresses numeric precision; follow-ups add travel buffers between experiences or a limit on the number of experiences.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Apr 2026; hack2hire 'Fill Layover With Experiences' (Medium, screening, 2026-06); InterviewDB 'Layover' phone-screen question

dsa.title: Consecutive numbers sum
dsa.statement: Count the ways a positive integer n can be written as a sum of one or more consecutive positive integers. Enumerate the run length k while k(k+1)/2 ≤ n and test divisibility; O(√n).
dsa.variant: Reported as a Hard screen problem in Apr 2026; follow-up asks to enumerate the actual runs.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Apr 2026 'Count Consecutive Positive Integer Sums'; 1point3acres list

dsa.title: Collatz sequence steps
dsa.statement: For a positive integer n, repeatedly apply n → n/2 if even else 3n+1 until reaching 1; return the number of steps. Then, for all integers ≤ N, find the one with the longest chain. Memoize chain lengths across calls (values can exceed N and overflow 32-bit ints), and discuss iterative vs recursive implementations and cache bounds.
dsa.variant: Follow-ups: streaming queries with a shared cache, bounding memory, and returning the full sequence.
dsa.evidence: hack2hire 'Collatz Sequence Steps' (Medium, screening, last reported 2026-10); listed as an Airbnb classic in the task brief

dsa.title: Find the median of a very large array
dsa.statement: Compute the median of an array too large to sort comfortably (or arriving as a stream). Discuss and implement one approach: quickselect for in-memory O(n) average; two heaps for a stream (LC 295); counting/bucket histogram when values are bounded; external partitioning when data exceeds memory. Handle even length and duplicates.
dsa.variant: Interviewer pushes on memory limits and on exactness vs approximation (t-digest).
dsa.evidence: hack2hire 'Find Median In Large Array' (Medium, screening, last reported 2026-10) — single aggregator source

dsa.title: Construct smallest number from I/D pattern (with digit constraints)
dsa.statement: Given a pattern of 'I'/'D' characters, build the lexicographically smallest digit string whose consecutive digits increase or decrease as the pattern says (stack-reversal greedy). A sibling screen asks for the smallest permutation-based number satisfying digit constraints, with care for leading zeros.
dsa.variant: Both appear as locked PracHub entries from Feb 2026.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Feb 2026 'Construct smallest number from I/D pattern' and 'Find smallest permutation under constraints'

dsa.title: Infection spread time on a grid (Rotting Oranges variant)
dsa.statement: A grid has empty cells, blocked cells and infected cells; each tick infection spreads to 4-neighbouring empty cells. Return how many ticks until every reachable empty cell is infected, or -1 if some empty cell can never be reached. Multi-source BFS.
dsa.variant: PracHub rates the Airbnb version Hard; follow-ups add multiple infection types or cells that resist for k ticks.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Mar 2026 'Infection Spread Time on a Grid'

dsa.title: Maximize sum with no adjacent tree nodes (House Robber III)
dsa.statement: Select nodes of a binary tree to maximize the sum of values with the rule that no two selected nodes are parent and child. Post-order DFS returning (take, skip) per node.
dsa.variant: Reported as a locked Hard entry in Jan 2026; follow-up may generalize to n-ary trees.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Jan 2026

dsa.title: Do two linked lists (possibly with cycles) share a node?
dsa.statement: Given two singly linked lists that may each contain a cycle, determine whether they share any node (by identity) and return the intersection node if they merge. Combine Floyd cycle detection with the classic intersection technique: if neither has a cycle use length alignment; if both do, check whether one list's cycle node is reachable from the other's cycle.
dsa.variant: Asked as the first half of an Apr 2026 screen whose second half was an iterator problem; Glassdoor reports a 'LeetCode-style linked-list medium' screen.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Jan 2026 (locked) and Apr 2026; Interview Query/Glassdoor summary; #10 in tag snapshot

dsa.title: Is the array a subsequence of the tree's inorder traversal? Then fix the tree minimally
dsa.statement: Given a binary tree and a target array, return whether the target is a subsequence of the tree's inorder sequence, in O(n) time and O(1) extra space (Morris traversal with a pointer into the target). Follow-up: if it is not, make the minimum number of node-value edits so that it becomes one.
dsa.variant: The O(1)-space requirement is the twist; the edit follow-up resembles LCS-style matching.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Aug 2025 and Sep 2025 entries

dsa.title: Allocate a refund across payment instruments by priority
dsa.statement: A booking was paid with several instruments (e.g. travel credit, gift card, coupon, credit card) each with a captured amount. Implement refund(amount) that distributes the refund across instruments following priority rules (refund non-cash/credit first or by a given ordering, proportional in some variants), never refunding more than was captured per instrument, supporting multiple partial refunds over time, and returning the per-instrument breakdown. Use integer minor units.
dsa.variant: Extended version is a 'refundable transaction ledger' processing a stream of payments and refunds with prioritization rules; probes on idempotent refund ids and rounding remainders.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Jul 2025 'Allocate refund across payments' (onsite), Jul 2025 'refundable transaction ledger', Sep 2025 'prioritized refund allocation engine'

dsa.title: Minimal set of listings to fit a group (minimize count, then wasted capacity)
dsa.statement: Listings in a neighbourhood each have a guest capacity (and price in some versions). Given a group size, choose a subset of listings whose total capacity is at least the group size, minimizing the number of listings first and total (or wasted) capacity second; return the chosen listings. Greedy by capacity fails on ties/waste, so use 0/1-knapsack DP over capacity for n up to ~1000.
dsa.variant: Vendor write-up frames the follow-up as 'what if n = 1000?' forcing the DP; PracHub's May 2026 'Find Optimal Property Combination' maximizes value under a capacity limit.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Sep 2025 'Find minimal property set in neighborhood' and May 2026; 1point3acres 'Choose Properties to Fit a Group with Minimal Waste'; vendor guide 'Listings Subset Optimization'

dsa.title: Tag / highlight keywords in review text (Add Bold Tag variant)
dsa.statement: Given review text and a dictionary mapping words/phrases to tags (e.g. 'san francisco' → city, 'airbnb' → business), wrap every occurrence as [tag]{original text}, matching case-insensitively while preserving original casing, preferring the longest match when phrases overlap, respecting word boundaries (possessive 'san's' tags only 'san'), and leaving everything else untouched. A 2026 variant 'redacts' phrases with simultaneous replacement against the original text.
dsa.variant: Pattern priority when tags overlap; trie or Aho-Corasick for many keys; 1point3acres lists 'Tag Matching and Annotation with Pattern Priority'.
dsa.evidence: LeetCode Discuss phone screen 'tag words'; InterviewDB 'Keyword Highlighting' phone screen; 1point3acres list (two entries); PracHub Sep 2026 redaction variant (MLE)

dsa.title: Fewest purchases/coins to hit an exact decimal target (Coin Change variant)
dsa.statement: Given denominations (or canister sizes / purchasable amounts) that may be decimals and a decimal target, return the minimum count that sums exactly to the target, or -1. Scale to integer units (cents/millilitres) first, then unbounded-knapsack DP; return the chosen items in the follow-up.
dsa.variant: Reported as 'Minimum Purchases to Fill an Exact Target Amount', 'Minimum Canisters to Top Up an Exact Target' and 'Decimal Coin Change' (2026).
dsa.evidence: PracHub Apr 2026 and Jun 2026 (MLE loops), 1point3acres SWE problem list

dsa.title: Minimum-cost set of service packages covering all required services
dsa.statement: Each package covers a set of services for a fixed price. Given the set of required services, pick packages (buying extra services is allowed) so every required service is covered at minimum total cost. With ≤ ~20 services, DP over the bitmask of covered services; discuss NP-hardness for large inputs.
dsa.variant: Follow-up: return the chosen packages and handle packages that are strictly dominated.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Jul 2025 'Compute minimum-cost service cover'

dsa.title: FIFO order allocator from oldest inventory batches
dsa.statement: Inventory arrives in batches with (reference id, received timestamp, quantity). Given an order quantity, allocate from the oldest batches first (tie-break by reference id), return the per-batch allocation and the remaining unfulfilled quantity, without mutating the input batches. Sort or heap by timestamp; handle zero-quantity batches and orders larger than stock.
dsa.variant: Follow-ups: many orders in sequence (keep a mutable copy), partial fulfilment policy, and unit tests for tie-breaks.
dsa.evidence: PracHub Aug 2026 'Allocate an Order from the Oldest Inventory Batches'; 1point3acres 'FIFO Order Allocator'

dsa.title: Reconstruct a traveller's itinerary from tickets
dsa.statement: Given (from, to) ticket pairs, rebuild the full trip that uses every ticket exactly once starting from a given airport, choosing the lexicographically smallest valid order. Hierholzer's algorithm with sorted adjacency lists.
dsa.variant: Described by a 2026 guide as a 'costume version of LC 332' seen in Airbnb coding rounds.
dsa.evidence: techinterview.org Airbnb guide (updated 2026-07), based on candidate reports from the past year

dsa.title: Can this date range be booked? (listing calendar insert)
dsa.statement: Maintain a listing's reservations and answer repeated 'can [check-in, check-out) be booked?' queries fast, inserting on success. Sorted interval list with binary search or a TreeMap keyed by start; discuss O(log n) per query.
dsa.variant: Follow-ups move toward concurrency: two guests booking the same range at once, idempotent retries — bridging into the booking system-design question.
dsa.evidence: techinterview.org guide (2026-07) describing a reported coding problem

dsa.title: Maximum concurrent bookings
dsa.statement: Given booking intervals (check-in, check-out), find the maximum number that overlap at any moment (and the moment it happens). Sweep line over sorted start/end events or min-heap of end times; be explicit about whether check-out day equals another booking's check-in day.
dsa.variant: Airbnb-flavoured Meeting Rooms II; follow-up asks for the busiest time window.
dsa.evidence: 1point3acres Airbnb problem list 'Maximum Concurrent Bookings' (2026-10)

dsa.title: Count connected regions in a grid, then a twist
dsa.statement: Count separate connected regions of marked cells in a grid (Number of Islands), then handle the interviewer's follow-up rule change (e.g. diagonal adjacency, cells added over time → union-find, or region size thresholds).
dsa.variant: Guides describe it as a warm-up before a Hard follow-up.
dsa.evidence: Design Gurus Airbnb guide (2026-09) unnamed example; codemia lists Number of Islands

dsa.title: LRU cache (coding-screen warm-up)
dsa.statement: Implement get/put with O(1) operations and least-recently-used eviction; then extend (TTL per key, size-aware eviction, or thread safety) as the interviewer layers requirements.
dsa.variant: Hello Interview lists LRU cache, a time-indexed iterator and a rate limiter as typical G8/G9 CoderPad screen problems 'with extensions'.
dsa.evidence: Hello Interview G8 and G9 guides (2026)

dsa.title: Zigzag / snake-order matrix print
dsa.statement: Print a matrix row by row alternating direction (left-to-right, then right-to-left). Follow-ups: do it without reversed() (manual two-pointer swap), print in spiral zigzag order using a direction array, and stream the output lazily with a generator for memory-sensitive inputs.
dsa.variant: Reported only by a vendor marketing page; treat as a plausible warm-up, not a bank staple.
dsa.evidence: Vendor guide (OA/VO service) CoderPad example

dsa.title: Minimum number of work sessions to finish the tasks
dsa.statement: Given task durations and a session length, find the minimum number of sessions needed when each task must fit entirely within one session. Bitmask DP over task subsets (n ≤ 14) or backtracking with pruning.
dsa.variant: Listed in a 2026 Blind/LeetCode post among 'the DP questions they asked' at Airbnb; the author did not confirm it was asked to them personally.
dsa.evidence: Blind 'Airbnb SWE interview breakdown: the DP questions they asked' + LeetCode mirror (2026)

dsa.title: Find the longest valid obstacle course at each position
dsa.statement: For each index i return the length of the longest non-decreasing subsequence ending at i. Patience-sorting with bisect_right in O(n log n).
dsa.variant: Same 2026 Blind/LeetCode DP list as above.
dsa.evidence: Blind + LeetCode offer post (2026)

dsa.title: Partition array into two arrays to minimize sum difference
dsa.statement: Split 2n integers into two equal-size halves minimizing |sum(A) − sum(B)|. Meet-in-the-middle: enumerate subset sums of each half grouped by size, then binary-search complementary sums.
dsa.variant: Same 2026 Blind/LeetCode DP list; practise as the 'Hard DP' tier Airbnb is known for.
dsa.evidence: Blind + LeetCode offer post (2026)

dsa.title: Execution order for dependent tasks (topological sort)
dsa.statement: Given N tasks and dependency pairs [a, b] meaning a must finish before b (an Airflow-style DAG), return a valid execution order or report a cycle. Kahn's algorithm or DFS post-order.
dsa.variant: Technical-screen warm-up in an India loop; codemia's 2026 guide lists Course Schedule among Airbnb coding questions.
dsa.evidence: LeetCode Discuss India experience (2021) + codemia guide (2026)

design.title: Design Airbnb's booking / reservation system (double-booking prevention)
design.prompt: Design the booking flow and availability store for Airbnb listings so two guests can never hold the same nights; include the API, data model and payment interaction. Often opened simply as 'design our booking system'.
probes: two guests booking the same listing in the same second — unique constraint/conditional insert vs SELECT FOR UPDATE vs optimistic version column vs SERIALIZABLE + retry
idempotency keys so a retried booking request is safe
reservation hold with expiry before payment capture; what the second guest sees
payment succeeded but reservation write failed (or vice versa) — outbox / saga / compensation
host calendar availability model and search index freshness (strong ledger vs eventually-consistent search)
schema and column data types (one G9 candidate was surprised by schema depth)
what breaks at 10x traffic; DB outage; monitoring and alerting
design.round: Architecture / system design (60 min), onsite; also the system-design screen for G9
design.evidence: Named as the canonical prompt by techinterview.org (2026-07), Hello Interview G8/G9 ('Reservation System for Airbnb'), PracHub Feb 2026 (760 solvers), TechPrep, SpaceComplexity, Design Gurus (2026-09)

design.title: Design Airbnb listing search
design.prompt: Design search over millions of listings with map-area/geo, date-availability, price and guest-count filters at low latency, including ranking.
probes: clarify QPS, listing count and number of filter dimensions
geo indexing (geohash / S2) and inverted index (Elasticsearch-style); sharding hot cities
how availability by date is combined with the index without scanning calendars
index freshness: event bus for listing/calendar updates, acceptable staleness (~seconds)
caching top query×city results; cache-miss storms
ranking on relevance, rating, price, booking history; personalization
failure modes: search node down, partial results, real-time inventory and partial availability as follow-up
design.evidence: Hello Interview G8 onsite example, Design Gurus probes (2026-09), vendor guide full walkthrough, codemia 'search and booking system', techinterview.org 'search and discovery'

design.title: Design host–guest messaging / group chat (with hot groups)
design.prompt: Design the real-time messaging backend between hosts and guests, supporting 1:1 and group threads at Airbnb scale; a 2026 variant emphasizes 'hot' groups (top-N most active group chats).
probes: WebSocket gateways and routing a message across many gateway servers
delivery guarantees, ordering within a thread, read receipts, multi-device sync
message persistence and history pagination; data model and indexes
detecting and optimizing hot groups (fan-out, caching, per-group sharding)
presence, push notifications when offline, automated host replies, translation
availability and disaster recovery trade-offs
design.evidence: PracHub Jan 2026 onsite experience ('design a group chat system', adapted WhatsApp design) and Jan 2026 'real-time chat with hot groups' (810 solvers); Hello Interview G8/G9; techinterview.org; earlier 2019 report

design.title: Design a waitlist for high-demand listings
design.prompt: Design a waitlist feature: when a listing is unavailable for requested dates a guest joins a waitlist scoped to listing+dates; when inventory frees up, notify waitlisted guests fairly without double-booking.
probes: API/schemas; ordering and fairness (FIFO vs priority tiers); dedup and idempotent joins
race between a cancellation freeing inventory and a direct booking — hold/claim semantics
notification fan-out, retries, exactly-once vs at-least-once
sharding by listing, spikes, backpressure, rate limiting
what breaks at 10x; graceful degradation; metrics/alerts after launch
design.evidence: PracHub Jul 2025 'hot-listing waitlist API'; Hello Interview G9 'Booking Waitlist System'; techinterview.org and TechPrep list it as a reported prompt

design.title: Design a scalable multi-channel notification system
design.prompt: Design a platform that delivers notifications (email, SMS, push, in-app) to millions of users reliably, with user preferences and rate limits.
probes: channel abstraction and provider failover
at-least-once delivery with dedup; idempotent sends
priority queues, batching, rate limiting per user/provider
preferences, quiet hours, localization
tracking delivery status and retries; observability
design.round: Architecture / system design (60 min); also the G8 design screen
design.evidence: PracHub Jul 2025 and Sep 2025 (two entries); Hello Interview G8/G9 'Design a Notification System'; Design Gurus 2026

design.title: Design a scalable job scheduler
design.prompt: Design an internal platform where services and engineers submit jobs to run at specified times or on schedules, at scale.
probes: durable job store and time-indexed scheduling; leader election vs partitioned workers
exactly-once execution vs at-least-once with idempotent jobs
retries, backoff, dead-letter handling, cancellation
priority and fairness across tenants; hot timestamps
monitoring lag, missed jobs, scaling workers
design.evidence: PracHub Apr 2026 (641 solvers); Hello Interview G8 and G9 common question

design.title: Design a reliable scheduler for one-time payment jobs
design.prompt: Design a scheduler for one-time payment jobs (e.g. host payouts at a future time) with durable claiming, retries, cancellation races, reconciliation and idempotency.
probes: claiming a job exactly once across workers (lease/CAS)
cancellation racing with execution
idempotent payment calls and reconciliation against the ledger
retry policy for transient vs permanent failures
design.evidence: PracHub Aug 2026 (locked)

design.title: Design a distributed key-value store
design.prompt: Design a distributed key-value store: API, partitioning, replication and request routing; a staff-level loop was told one architecture round would be a 'database key-value store'.
probes: consistent hashing and rebalancing
replication and consistency model (quorum, leader vs leaderless)
request routing/coordinator, hinted handoff, read repair
failure detection and recovery; hot keys
design.evidence: PracHub Jan 2026 (locked); Blind staff-engineer architecture thread (2022)

design.title: Design a user-event aggregation system
design.prompt: Design a system that ingests user events and serves aggregated metrics; cover the API, database choice, monitoring and SLOs.
probes: at-least-once vs exactly-once aggregation and dedup
which store holds aggregates and how it is queried
streaming vs batch; late events; windowing
SLO definition and monitoring

design.evidence: 1point3acres onsite write-up (interviews Jul–Sep 2024, posted Feb 2025)

design.title: Design a rental watchlist with availability-change notifications
design.prompt: Users watch listings and get notified when availability or price changes for their dates.
probes: change detection from calendar/pricing updates (CDC/event stream) vs polling
matching changes to many watchers efficiently (inverted index by listing/date)
notification dedup and throttling
consistency between watchlist state and listing state
design.evidence: PracHub Sep 2025 (761 solvers)

design.title: Design a fast host listings metrics page
design.prompt: A host with 100+ listings picks a date range and must see nights booked and average price per listing; the current page is slow. Design APIs, storage, indexing, caching/precomputation given Listings, Reservations and Pricing tables.
probes: time-range aggregation correctness with reservations partially overlapping the range and cancellations
precomputed daily rollups vs on-demand queries; keeping rollups current
indexing strategy and pagination
defining and validating latency goals
design.evidence: PracHub Dec 2025

design.title: Design the split-stay combinations API
design.prompt: Design an HTTP endpoint that, given a date range and listings with availability, returns valid two-listing split stays (the design twin of the split-stay coding problem).
probes: request/response schema, availability encoding, error payloads
avoiding an O(L²·N) scan: prefix/suffix coverage, bitsets, precomputed availability runs
dedup of unordered pairs and multiple valid switch days
ranking (price, rating, distance, balance) and deterministic cursor pagination
edge cases: min nights per segment, cleaning-day gaps, time zones
caching/freshness at large supply, idempotency and rate limiting
design.evidence: PracHub Sep 2025 (780 solvers)

design.title: Design an A/B testing (experimentation) platform
design.prompt: Design a platform to define experiments and consistently assign eligible users to control/treatment, then collect metrics.
probes: deterministic bucketing (hash of user+experiment), exposure logging
mutually exclusive layers and traffic allocation changes
eligibility rules and guardrail metrics
stats pipeline and result freshness

design.prompt: Design a scalable, low-latency backend for a global vacation-rental marketplace (search + feed + booking fundamentals).

search/feed systems and their consistency with inventory
service decomposition and failure isolation

design.prompt: Design a Twitter-like feed system — the architecture prompt reported from a Bengaluru loop.

timeline cache and pagination

lld.title: CodeSignal OA: in-memory cloud storage / file system with users, quotas and compression
lld.prompt: Level 1: add/get/copy files by name and size. Level 2: search files by prefix and suffix (ranked deterministically). Level 3: add users with capacity, add files on behalf of a user, update capacity, make copy fail when it would exceed remaining capacity (earlier levels assume an admin user), merge accounts. Level 4: compress/decompress a file (size halves; consumed capacity must update) or per-user backup/restore with conflict handling.
lld.deliverable: Working class implementation passing hidden tests per level within ~90 min; tests cannot be edited
probes: Level 3 forces changes to Level 1–2 code — keep file ownership and sizes in one model
exact capacity accounting after copy/compress
deterministic ordering in search results
largest-file queries and account merges
lld.evidence: PracHub experiences Aug 2026 ('passed L3, out of time on L4'), Glassdoor Jul–Aug 2026 ('build a cloud storage mechanism'), 1point3acres OA threads Aug 2026, PracHub question entries Aug 2026 (three variants)

lld.title: CodeSignal OA: in-memory banking system (transfers, top spenders, scheduled payments, merges, historical balances)
lld.prompt: Level 1: create_account / deposit / transfer with timestamps and many edge cases (unknown account, self-transfer, insufficient funds, duplicates). Level 2: top_spenders(n) ranked by outgoing total with ties broken by account id. Level 3: schedule a payment for a future timestamp, cancel it, query its state; due payments must execute before any later operation at that timestamp and update spending totals. Level 4: merge accounts preserving balances, history, spending and scheduled payments (aliases → canonical account), or answer historical balance at a timestamp.
lld.deliverable: Class implementation passing hidden tests per level
probes: event ordering by timestamp (process due scheduled payments first)
tie-breaking in rankings — a plain heap is not enough
what old account ids mean after a merge
centralized account state vs scattered dicts
lld.evidence: PracHub Aug 2026 experience; PracHub 'Four-Level Banking System OA, stuck on Level 3 at 440' ; 1point3acres 'Progressive Banking System Challenge' Aug 2026; PracHub question entries Jul–Sep 2026; LeetCode 2043 Simple Bank System is the public analogue

lld.title: CodeSignal OA: task management system with quotas and expiring assignments
lld.prompt: Level 1: add, update and retrieve tasks. Level 2: search tasks by name and list tasks sorted by priority. Level 3: users with task quotas and time-based assignments that expire automatically. Level 4: complete assigned tasks and report overdue assignments.
lld.deliverable: Class implementation passing hidden tests per level; proctored with screen share + mic
probes: quota enforcement at assignment time
expiry evaluated lazily by timestamp on each call
state transitions (assigned → completed / expired / overdue) and deterministic reports
lld.evidence: PracHub Sep 2026 experience (auto-sent OA); 1point3acres OA thread Sep 2026; PracHub question entries Jul and Sep 2026

lld.title: CodeSignal OA: working-hours register with promotions and double-pay periods
lld.prompt: Level 1: add employees, badge in/out, total hours worked. Level 2: sort employees by hours and return top n. Level 3: promotions take effect at the employee's next badge-in (pending until then) and salary is computed in segments using the rate in effect per session. Level 4: a grant period during which any shift fully inside it is paid double; report total double pay issued.
lld.deliverable: Class implementation passing hidden tests per level in 90 min
probes: delayed state transitions (pending promotion)
per-session salary segments as rates change
interval containment for the double-pay window
lld.evidence: PracHub Jul 2026 experience and question entry

lld.title: CodeSignal OA: in-memory object/parcel attribute store with compare-and-set, prefix scan and TTL
lld.prompt: Build a nested hash-map store of objects with fields: set/get/delete fields, conditional (compare-and-set) updates, list keys/fields by prefix in deterministic order, and TTL expiry on fields or objects evaluated against the operation timestamp; later levels add filtering and backup/restore. The Hello Interview 'in-memory key-value store with expiration' coding-screen problem is the same core.
lld.deliverable: Class implementation passing hidden tests per level (OA) or runnable code in a 60-min screen
probes: lazy vs eager expiry and timestamp-driven cleanup
prefix scan ordering
CAS semantics on missing fields
scores like 410/600 reported — later levels are where candidates stall
lld.round: Online assessment (CodeSignal ICA); also coding screen

lld.title: Code Review round: review three pull requests
lld.prompt: Read a small service repo for context, then review ~3 PRs of increasing complexity and write comments as for a teammate. Reported PR 1: a fix for an API sending the wrong consistency value ('WEAK' instead of EVENTUAL/STRONG) — points: use an Enum, test every value, don't swallow exceptions, log/alert, f-strings. PR 2: a new DAO layer fetching listing/host data from downstream services with retries — points: dict[key] KeyError vs .get(), reraise instead of catch-all, unit tests for retries, shared retry base class, Optional type hints, slots on frozen dataclasses, async. PR 3: larger change (details paywalled). Other loops report planted off-by-one, null dereference, injection/authorization flaws, duplicated logic and misleading names.
lld.deliverable: Written review comments prioritized by severity, with suggested fixes; sometimes with the interviewer silent
probes: correctness first, then security, then maintainability/style
merge-blocking vs follow-up
explaining why each issue matters
speed — 60 min is tight for 3 PRs
Python/Go/Java variants share structure
